newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CHAMPION BRAVES FACE STORIED YANKEES IN WORLD SERIES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CHAMPION BRAVES FACE STORIED YANKEES IN WORLD SERIES.

text.p: The Atlanta Braves roar into the World Series on Saturday with the confidence of champions riding a juggernaut, but the New York Yankees have a little destiny and a whole lot of history on their side.
The Braves now have reached four of the last five World Series.
"We're going back," exulted third baseman Chipper Jones after clinching over the St Louis Cardinals in the National League Championship Series Thursday night. "It's unbelievable."

Atlanta had to come back from a 3-1 deficit in the NLCS to earn the right to defend its only championship. The Braves staved off elimination in St Louis with a 14-0 Game 5 romp, and capped it at home with a post-season record 15-0 avalanche in Game 7, outscoring the Cards 32-1 over the final three.

But the Yankees also have a feeling that everything is going their way. Not only did they gather momentum with their 4-1 American League Championship Series win over the Baltimore Orioles, they got some help from unexpected sources.

A 12-year-old fan's intervention and an umpire's mistake, a bizarre throwaway on a fake throw by Todd Zeile and a ball scooting through beleaguered superstar Roberto Alomar's legs were some of the little extras that helped the Yanks.
"It was a destiny thing," said left fielder Tim Raines.

There is destiny, and then there is history. The Yankees, with 22 championships, will be making their 34th World Series appearance. They lead both categories by wide margins. This will be their first Series in 15 years. They last won in 1978.
The Yankees, the highest-paid team in baseball, were led by ALCS Most Valuable Player and emerging superstar Bernie Williams.

Playing with a quiet elegance that has already evoked a few comparisons to Yankee legend and fellow centre fielder Joe DiMaggio, Williams hit safely in all nine post-season games, tied an A.L. playoff record with five home runs and added sparkling fielding and daring base-running.

Other Yankees also found some of the old Bronx Bomber power after a regular season in which the team hit the third fewest home runs (162) in the American League. They smacked a record-tying 10 in the ALCS. Darryl Strawberry and Cecil Fielder each hit three in the post-season.
Strawberry has a small bone fracture in his right big toe. "My mind is set on playing in the World Series," he insisted, but it remained to be seen how he would be used.
If Strawberry can't play the field and must be used as designated hitter in New York, Raines might get his regular job in left back. Fielder might bump Tino Martinez at first.
In Atlanta, the National League city, the lack of the designated hitter spot could force even tougher decisions on manager Joe Torre.
The Braves, highest-paid team in the National League, were led by NLCS Most Valuable Player Javier Lopez. The catcher hit a record .542 and had a record-tying 13 hits in the series.
"This is a dream," said Lopez. "This is amazing."
Starting pitching is where Atlanta appears to have an edge but, noted manager Bobby Cox, "Not only did we pitch well, we hit the ball awfully well."

But it is their pitching that scares people most. John Smoltz is a lock for National League Cy Young winner this season. Greg Maddux is history's only four-time Cy Young winner and Tom Glavine, who clinched the Series last year and the league pennant this year, had the last Cy Young year before Maddux.
For New York, Andy Pettitte, the probable A.L. Cy Young winner and Smoltz's likely opponent in Game 1, threw eight fine innings in Game 5 against Baltimore after two subpar post-season starts.
Normally gritty David Cone also has looked shaky at times as he continues to recover from an aneurysm in his right arm. Jimmy Key threw well in the Yankees' Game 3 ALCS victory.

The Yankees' bullpen has been superb. Set-up man Mariano Rivera (1-0, 0.000 ERA, 8.2 innings) and closer John Wetteland (3 saves, 2.25 ERA, 8.0 innings) are the best one-two punch in baseball, and four other relievers combined for four wins this post-season.
Atlanta closer Mark Wohlers has been impeccable in the post-season, getting five saves without yielding a run.
The last time the two clubs met was in 1957-58, when the Braves were in Milwaukee. The Braves won in 1957 and the Yankees in 1958.
Torre is believed to have waited longer to go to a World Series than anyone else -- 4,272 games in uniform as a player and manager.
"Now you can go into the World Series and enjoy yourself, throw caution to the wind and have some fun," said the Yankee manager.
